newsitem.title: CHINA: China to export 50,000 T corn to S.Korea - source.
newsitem.headline: China to export 50,000 T corn to S.Korea - source.

text.p: China will export a single shipment of 50,000 tonnes of corn to South Korea in the next few days, the largest such shipment since a ban on corn exports was lifted last year, an industry source said on Friday.

The deal in effect eases curbs on large single shipments of corn that had remained in force after smaller shipments were permitted last year. China halted corn exports in late 1994 amid soaring domestic prices.
"This deal is because there is an oversupply of corn, supply exceeds demand," the source said. "This export will help to stabilise domestic prices."
Bulk shipments would cut shipping costs and make Chinese corn exports more competitive, he said.
The China National Cereals, Oils and Foodstuff Import and Export Corp, which has a monopoly on corn exports, was the seller, said the source, who declined to be identified.
The corn would be exported from China's northeastern port city of Dalian, the source said.

South Korea has been the leading buyer of Chinese corn in 1997, with purchases reaching an estimate 1.2 million tonnes so far and projected to rise to 2.0 million tonnes by the end of September. -- Beijing Newsroom (8610) 6532 1921
